group.title: Phones, media and news
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A machine or tool for a special purpose, like a phone.
examples: Please turn off all {devices} during the test.
wrong: A device is a kind of plant.

words.meaning: A program you download onto a phone or tablet.
examples: I use an {app} to learn words.
wrong: An app is a cable for your charger.

words.meaning: To put electricity into a battery.
wrong: I charged my phone, so the battery is empty.

words.meaning: To put a program on a computer or phone so it is ready to use.
wrong: I installed the app, so it isn’t on my phone.

words.meaning: To remove something from a computer or phone.
wrong: I deleted the file to keep it safe forever.

words.meaning: To look for information, often online.
wrong: I searched for the answer by closing my eyes.

words.meaning: A word or picture on a web page that takes you to another page.
wrong: A link is a kind of keyboard.

words.meaning: A set of details that lets you use a website or app.
wrong: An account is the screen of your phone.

words.meaning: To put a message or photo online.
examples: She {posted} a photo of her dog.
wrong: I posted the photo, so nobody can see it online.

words.meaning: Something you say or write that gives an opinion.
examples: He left a nice {comment} under my video.
wrong: A comment is a song without any words.

words.meaning: A person who chooses to see someone’s posts online.
wrong: A follower is a person who never sees your posts.

words.meaning: A recorded talk show you can listen to online.
examples: I listen to a science {podcast} on the bus.
wrong: A podcast is a kind of printed magazine.

words.meaning: A TV station, or a set of videos by one person online.
wrong: A channel is a kind of remote control.

words.meaning: Large printed pages with news, sold every day.
examples: My father reads the {newspaper} at breakfast.
wrong: A newspaper is a radio show.

words.meaning: A person who writes news for a newspaper, website or TV.
examples: A {journalist} asked the mayor some questions.
wrong: A journalist is a person who never writes anything.

words.meaning: The title of a news story, in large letters.
examples: The {headline} said the team had won.
wrong: A headline is the smallest text at the bottom of a page.

words.meaning: A piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
examples: I read an interesting {article} about sleep.
wrong: An article is a kind of TV.

words.meaning: To send out a program on TV or radio.
wrong: They broadcast the show, so nobody could watch it.

words.meaning: To watch or listen to something online without downloading it.
wrong: I streamed the film on a CD player with no internet.

words.meaning: A show on TV or radio; or a set of instructions for a computer.
wrong: A program is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: To enter your name and password to use a website or app.
wrong: I logged in by turning off the computer.

words.meaning: To send a written message by phone.
wrong: I texted her by shouting across the street.

words.meaning: A message from an app that tells you something new.
examples: I got a {notification} about the delivery.
wrong: A notification is the charger for your phone.

words.meaning: The choices that control how a device or app works.
wrong: Settings is a kind of game you play online.

words.meaning: To press a button on a mouse or touch a link.
wrong: I clicked the link with my foot on the floor.

words.meaning: To move text up or down on a screen.
wrong: I scrolled down the page of a paper book.

words.meaning: Not connected to the internet.
wrong: I was offline, so I sent emails all day.

words.meaning: Spreading quickly online to many people.
examples: The video went {viral} in one day.
wrong: The video went viral, so nobody saw it.

words.meaning: A website where a person writes regularly about their life or ideas.
wrong: A blog is a kind of mobile phone.

words.meaning: To sign up to get something regularly, like a magazine or channel.
examples: {Subscribe} to get new videos every week.
wrong: I subscribed to the channel, so I never get its videos.

words.meaning: Using computers and electronic data.
wrong: A digital clock has no electricity or screen.

words.meaning: A way of connecting to the internet without wires.
examples: Is there free {wifi} in the hotel?
wrong: Wifi is a long cable you plug into the wall.

words.meaning: A picture of what is on your screen.
examples: Send me a {screenshot} of the error.
wrong: A screenshot is a broken screen.

words.meaning: A set of keys you press together to do something quickly.
examples: Use a {keyboard shortcut} to copy text.
wrong: A keyboard shortcut is the longest way to do something.

words.meaning: A thin book with articles and pictures, sold every week or month.
wrong: A magazine is a TV channel.

words.meaning: To ask someone questions for a newspaper, TV or a job.
wrong: She interviewed him without asking a single question.

words.meaning: Information about recent events.
wrong: The news is a report about things that will never happen.

words.meaning: The people who watch or listen to a show.
wrong: The audience is the person who sings on stage.

words.meaning: A short film or picture that tries to sell something.
examples: There are too many {adverts} on TV.
wrong: An advert is a news report with no products in it.

words.meaning: The right to keep your personal life secret.
examples: Check the {privacy} settings on your account.
wrong: Privacy means sharing everything about yourself with everyone.
